arxiv-2008-01938.title: Solving Dynamic Programming Problem by Pipeline Implementation on GPU
arxiv-2008-01938.creator: Susumu Matsumae, Makoto Miyazaki
arxiv-2008-01938.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Susumu Matsumae, Makoto Miyazaki. In this paper, we show the effectiveness of a pipeline implementation of Dynamic Programming (DP) on GPU. As an example, we explain how to solve a matrix-chain multiplication (MCM) problem by DP on GPU.

arxiv-2303-12259.title: Brain-inspired bodily self-perception model for robot rubber hand illusion
arxiv-2303-12259.creator: Yuxuan Zhao, Enmeng Lu, Yi Zeng
arxiv-2303-12259.description: Abstract At the core of bodily self-consciousness is the perception of the ownership of one’s body. Recent efforts to gain a deeper understanding of the mechanisms behind the brain’s encoding of the self-body have led to various attempts to develop a unified theoretical framework to explain related behavioral and neurophysiological phenomena.

arxiv-2502-12609.title: New Crouzeix-Raviart elements of even degree: theoretical aspects, numerical performance, and applications to the Stokes’ equations
arxiv-2502-12609.creator: A. Bressan, L. Mascotto, M. Mosconi
arxiv-2502-12609.description: Abstract We construct new Crouzeix-Raviart (CR) spaces of even degree p p that are spanned by basis functions mimicking those for the odd degree case. Compared to the standard CR gospel, the present construction allows for the use of nested bases of increasing degree and is particularly suited to design variable order CR methods.

pmc-10572759.title: The Relationship between Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Functional Tests Assessment in Patients with Lumbar Disk Hernia
pmc-10572759.creator: Bogdan-Alexandru Antohe, Hüseyin Şahin Uysal, Adelina-Elena Panaet, George-Sebastian Iacob, Marinela Rață, Young-Chang Arai
pmc-10572759.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings are the gold standard for diagnosing herniated discs, there are many limitations to accessing MRI scanning devices in practice. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between functional tests (the visual analog scale (VAS), the SLUMP test, the Sciatica Bothersomeness Index (SBI), the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and the LASEGUE test and MRI findings (LSA, IVDH L4-L5, IVDH L5-S1, DHS L4-L5, and DHS L5-S1) in patients diagnosed with disc herniation.

pmc-10714450.title: Bleeding risk factors and real-world antithrombotic therapies in elderly patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a retrospective study
pmc-10714450.creator: Kanako Fujita, Noriko Kohyama, Miki Sato, Tomokazu Deguchi, Hiroshi Suzuki, Mio Ebato, Mari Kogo
pmc-10714450.description: BackgroundBleeding risk factors in elderly patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are unclear and data on the use of antithrombotic drugs are lacking. We investigated the bleeding risk factors in elderly patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing PCI to help optimize antithrombotic therapy according to bleeding risk.

pmc-10739536.title: ACCEPTABILITY OF HIGH-INTENSITY FUNCTIONAL STRENGTH TRAINING AT HOME FOR POSTINJURY OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10739536.creator: Ashley Morgan, Jennifer Heisz, Ada Tang, Lehana Thabane, Julie Richardson
pmc-10739536.description: Regular exercise plays a vital role in optimizing aging and preventing functional decline. Despite the recognized benefit of exercise, adherence is challenging, and acceptability of exercise interventions is crucial. Acceptability is influenced by various factors, including content, context, and delivery.

pmc-11306126.title: Daily life participation in PTSD: pilot study on patterns and correlators
pmc-11306126.creator: Ruth Shapira, Yisca Jessica Baris Ginat, Lena Lipskaya-Velikovsky
pmc-11306126.description: IntroductionParticipation in daily life activities with both the personal and community meaning is an important component of health and well-being. Even though there are mounting reports on the challenges in various aspects of daily-life functioning among individuals with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), to date little research has been conducted on their comprehensive patterns of participation.

pmc-11363893.title: Aortoenteric Fistula with Digestive Contrast Material Leaking in the Aneurysmal Sac
pmc-11363893.creator: Quentin Conroux, Emmanuel Agneessens, Vincent Scavee
pmc-11363893.description: Teaching point: Aortoenteric fistula, a major complication of aortic surgery, can be identified with certainty on CT scan with opacification of the intestinal tract. Case History A 58-year-old male patient with an aorto-biiliac graft presented to the emergency department with diffuse back and abdominal pain.

pmc-12655856.title: Current Insights into the Phytochemistry and Pharmacological Properties of Ruscus aculeatus
pmc-12655856.creator: Wiktoria Pacuła, Ireneusz Sowa, Marcin Feldo, Filip Graczyk, Rafał Patryn, Magdalena Wójciak
pmc-12655856.description: Ruscus aculeatus L. (butcher’s broom), a member of the Asparagaceae family, is a perennial shrub native to the Mediterranean and Black Sea regions and naturalized in parts of Europe and North America. Traditionally, the rhizome and root of this species have been employed in folk medicine for the treatment of venous insufficiency, hemorrhoids, edema, and various dermatological and urinary ailments.

pmc-12745425.title: Spatio-temporal distribution and aggregation analysis of road traffic fatalities in Shandong Province, China, 2012–2022
pmc-12745425.creator: Tao Wang, Zi-Long Lu, Jie Chu, Qi Li, Zhi-ying Yao, Xiao-Lei Guo, Cun-Xian Jia
pmc-12745425.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to analyze the temporal and spatial distribution, as well as spatio-temporal aggregation, of road traffic fatalities in Shandong Province, China, from 2012 to 2022, with the aim of establishing scientific foundation for crafting customized intervention strategies and preventive actions to mitigate road traffic fatalities.

pmc-13039484.title: Neuroinflammation and NeuroHIV: understanding the role of HIV-1 related factors in microglial activation
pmc-13039484.creator: Jinfang Zhao, Fan Bu, Hui Wu, Jiayi He, Jiaye Liu
pmc-13039484.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). NeuroHIV has emerged as a significant unmet challenge, manifesting as impairments in learning, memory, sensorimotor, and language in people living with HIV (PLWH). Despite the widespread use of antiretroviral therapy, the incidence of NeuroHIV remains high among PLWH. Microglial cells, as the main targets and reservoirs for HIV-1 infection, play crucial roles in sustaining HIV-1 persistence and contributing to neuroinflammation and neuroHIV pathogenesis.
